column1: # Step 1's eight pairs, and the draw of which arm is shown as A in the first call. Both
# orderings are always run, so the draw decides presentation order only, never what is compared.
# Drawn once with python random.seed(20260909); reproduce it before changing a row.
# p9 and p10 are the positive control. The ground-truth tests already rank head2 last of the
# five: 62/65, and it never opened stores/convex/src/server/index-map.ts. That ranking comes
# from running tests, not from the grader, so asking the grader to place head2 against the two
# other proxied arms asks it a question whose answer is already known from outside it.
# Drawn with python random.seed(20260910); reproduce it before changing a row.
# p11 shows the grader the same change on both sides (control2b is a byte-identical copy of
# control2 under another token). It must come out Yes/Yes. No pair in p1–p8 did, so this is
# the test that the grader can say "same" at all.
